findings.resolution: The share count and reconstruction threshold apply separately to each client's private-mask seed (rd_seed) and first private key (sk1), which derives pairwise masks. The client creates shares of both with create_shares(secret, threshold, share_num). During upstream unmasking, the server reconstructs active clients' private-mask seeds or dropped clients' first private keys. The project's strict wrapper independently requires the full cohort at every stage, so the reconstruction threshold does not authorise continuing with only two client replies.

findings.suggested_full_paragraph_old: Secure aggregation comprised four stages: setup, key sharing, masked-vector collection and unmasking. The server used SecAggPlusWorkflow and clients used secaggplus_mod, with stage identifiers setup, share_keys, collect_masked_vectors and unmask. Message checks verified expected fields and the absence of plaintext individual updates in aggregation replies. The configured share count was three and the reconstruction threshold was two. Nevertheless, every accepted stage required replies from all three clients. Missing replies stopped the workflow, with no fallback to ordinary FedAvg.
findings.suggested_full_paragraph_new: Secure aggregation comprised four stages: setup, key sharing, masked-vector collection and unmasking. The server used SecAggPlusWorkflow and clients used secaggplus_mod, with stage identifiers setup, share_keys, collect_masked_vectors and unmask. Message checks verified expected fields and the absence of plaintext individual updates in aggregation replies. The configured share count was three and the reconstruction threshold was two for each client's private-mask seed and the private key used to derive pairwise masks: the count sets how many shares are created, and the threshold sets how many are needed to reconstruct the respective secret for unmasking. Nevertheless, every accepted stage required replies from all three clients. Missing replies stopped the workflow, with no fallback to ordinary FedAvg.

findings.resolution: The legacy-fold control constructs distinct public byte seeds whose repeated little-endian words cancel in the old helper's XOR reduction to its RandomState seed. The executed assertions required identical legacy output arrays and distinct candidate output arrays for these constructed seeds. Agreement means each implementation met this deliberately different expected result. The separate public-output checks compare HMAC against a fixed vector and the PRG arrays against an independently written scalar decoder for each specified modulus.
evidence_limits: This is a constructed seed-folding control. It does not estimate general collision rates or prove collision resistance, entropy, unpredictability or privacy.
The proposed wording retains the existing runtime-file count and modulus count; it introduces no new numerical result.

findings.suggested_full_paragraph_new: 424 installed Flower runtime files matched the candidate wheel. Public-vector outputs and the checks over 15 moduli matched their respective reference outputs. The constructed legacy-fold control confirmed identical output arrays from the previous helper for distinct public seeds chosen to collapse under its seed reduction, and distinct output arrays from the candidate helper.

findings.resolution: The executed fixture directly passed current_stage=Stage.SHARE_KEYS and configs={Key.STAGE:Stage.SETUP} to the installed check_stage function. That function permits a requested SETUP and logs a warning when the current stage is not UNMASK. The fixture returned without exception, with zero aggregate callbacks. Separately, the installed message handler would assign SETUP and call _setup after config validation. _setup reloads the supplied protocol parameters, clears rd_seed_share_dict, sk1_share_dict and ss2_dict, and generates both private/public key pairs anew. The fixture did not execute that state reset.

findings.resolution: The compared categories are exact public-key bytes, private-key bytes, private-mask seed bytes, pairwise mask-key bytes, share-encryption-key bytes and ordered tuples of serialized masked-parameter byte strings. The finite in-memory set-cardinality checks found no repeated value within each category.
evidence_limits: Exact comparisons took place only in memory. Retained JSON contains counts and booleans, not the actual secret values or their digests; those values cannot be independently recovered from the retained JSON.
No reuse within a finite checked category is not proof of entropy, unpredictability or privacy. The check directly exercised installed setup/share/collect functions and did not run UNMASK.
Each pair is counted once, despite checking agreement at both endpoints; equality is checked within each category, not between categories.
findings.suggested_full_paragraph_old: Across 20 three-client sessions, none of the compared generated contexts was reused within its category. This finite check does not prove entropy or unpredictability.

This finite check does not prove entropy or unpredictability.

findings.suggested_full_paragraph_old: The test harness used a toy strategy and a replica client guard adapted to the public inputs to exercise installed Flower code and named project validators. Three public reference cases with known expected outputs used the upstream workflow/client path. Selected direct cases called actual project methods before any data or model access. The standard-FedAvg control used a native plain Flower reply, not the complete benchmark application. In SV-07, the observer and capsule functions were actual project code, but measurement_scope() used a public substitute. The cases therefore did not all test the complete application from end to end, which limits their coverage of application and network behaviour.
findings.suggested_full_paragraph_new: The test harness used a toy strategy and a replica client guard adapted to the public inputs to exercise installed Flower code and named project validators. Three public reference cases with known expected outputs used the upstream workflow/client path. Selected direct cases called actual project methods before any data or model access. The standard-FedAvg control used a native plain Flower reply, not the complete benchmark application. In SV-07, the project observer functions wrote message-content byte counts, timings and permitted metadata; the failure-capsule function exported selected error, traceback-frame and round metadata. Their JSON outputs were checked for injected public canaries. The harness replaced measurement_scope() with a dictionary of public round, condition, stage and configuration-digest values, bypassing its normal reading and validation of the job-specific bundled measurement configuration. The cases therefore did not all test the complete application from end to end, which limits their coverage of application and network behaviour.

Set cardinalities were compared with the prespecified expected counts, and reverse endpoint key derivations were checked for equality.

findings.suggested_full_paragraph_old: SV-06 checked whether generated protocol contexts were reused across twenty independent three-client sessions. The same public NumPy seed, 177, was reset for each session. In-memory comparisons found 120 distinct public-key representations and 120 distinct private-key representations. Within their respective categories, there were 60 self-seed contexts, 60 pairwise mask-key contexts, 60 share-encryption-key contexts and 60 masked-reply contexts. Matching peers derived matching keys. The installed setup/share/collect functions ran. Checking reuse of these contexts did not require UNMASK, so that stage was not run in this group. SV-02 contains complete four-stage numerical checks. Observing no reuse in a finite check does not establish entropy or unpredictability.
